query: Consider the following context: High entropy alloys have excellent wear resistance, so they have great application prospects in the fields of wear resistance and surface protection. In that context, which material can be used for adhere to the surface of a Cu matrix, and why?

generation.hypothesis: A nanocrystalline refractory high-entropy alloy (RHEA) film can adhere to the surface of a Cu matrix due to its excellent interface properties, resulting in enhanced wear resistance.
generation.material_initial_state: Cu matrix in its pure form
generation.intervention: Deposition of a nanocrystalline RHEA film on the Cu matrix surface
generation.conditions: Room temperature, atmospheric pressure, and a film thickness of 1-5 micrometers
generation.structural_mediator: Interface between the RHEA film and the Cu matrix
generation.mechanism: The nanocrystalline RHEA film's high entropy and refractory nature enhance its interface properties, allowing for strong adhesion to the Cu matrix and resulting in improved wear resistance
generation.predicted_outcome: An increase in wear resistance of at least 30% compared to the bare Cu matrix, measured in terms of volume loss per unit distance (mm^3/m)
generation.baseline: Bare Cu matrix without any coating or film
generation.boundary: A minimum film thickness of 1 micrometer and a maximum film thickness of 5 micrometers
generation.uncertainty: The actual wear resistance improvement may vary depending on the specific RHEA composition, film thickness, and deposition method used

falsification_experiment.design: Sliding wear test using a ball-on-disk tribometer
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the wear resistance of the RHEA-coated Cu matrix is not at least 30% higher than the bare Cu matrix, the hypothesis is falsified, with a threshold of 20% increase in wear resistance (i.e., if the improvement is less than 20%, the hypothesis is rejected)
